newsitem.title: CANADA: Pipelines, processing bolster TCPL Q1.
newsitem.headline: Pipelines, processing bolster TCPL Q1.

text.p: TransCanada PipeLines Ltd, which earlier reporter higher first-quarter earnings, said on Wednesday its fortunes were bolstered by growth in its pipelines and energy processing divisions.
TransCanada reported net income of C$105.2 million or C$0.48 a share in the first quarter, up from C$91.8 million or C$0.45 a share in the same period last year.
Revenues for the firm, which operates Canada's main corss-country natural gas pipeline, totalled C$3.65 billion, up from C$2.28 billion in the first quarter of 1996.

TransCanada said net earnings from its energy transmission division totalled C$78 million in the quarter, up 4.1 percent from the year-earlier period. Of that, the Canadian mainline contributed C$61 million.
The company's share of earnings from its other North American oil and natural gas pipeline investments rose C$3.7 million to C$17 million, it said.
Net earnings from TransCanada's energy processing arm totalled C$20.9 million in the period, up from C$8.1 million in the first quarter of 1996.

TransCanada said the increase reflected its acquisition of the remaining shares of Alberta Natural Gas Co Ltd in March 1996, as well as the start-up of two Ontario-based electric generation plants in November and purchase of a U.S.-based gas liquids processing business in February.

The company's Canadian mainline delivered 677.3 billion cubic feet of natural gas in the first quarter, up from 651.7 Bcf in 1996, it said. Peak day delivery during the first quarter was 8.2 BCF on January 17, compared to a peak day of 7.8 Bcf on January 15, 1996.
Natural gas marketing sales were 445.2 BCF in the quarter, a jump from 343.3 BCF in the same period last year.
Crude oil, refined products and natural gas liquids sales totalled 46.6 million barrels of crude oil, up from 28.4 million barrels in the first quarter of 1996, TransCanada said.
